Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate contains a short video that appears to demonstrate the Visual Intelligence feature of Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Let's take a look together.

macOS 26.7 contains demo video of camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered a short video in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate, showing a man wearing AirPods seemingly asking Siri to record the book he's reading, with Siri's voiceover stating:

The video doesn't show the camera itself, and the earbuds' appearance is very similar to the current AirPods Pro, with the most noticeable difference being that the stem looks slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris also posted the same video on the X platform:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods within this year, with the internal codename B790. Earlier, MacRumors also found B790-related information in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, including code for "image streaming."

Interestingly, these AirPods are reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model with the internal codename B798, which is expected to launch in 2027.

Judging from Apple's decision to hide this demo video in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to make their official debut at next month's iPhone launch event.

What are your thoughts on this video? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
